title: Day 1 Teaching Lab — Governance Decision Tabletop
objective: Study-guide review — Day 1 — Governance, Compliance, Risk, and AI Governance: Day 1 Teaching Lab — Governance Decision Tabletop.

blocks.text: Use this lab to fill a 45-minute block and force students to practice governance language.

Scenario: a business unit wants to launch a customer analytics initiative. It will ingest production customer data, send selected fields to a third-party platform, use an AI assistant for summaries, and present dashboard metrics to executives.

rows: Policy intent, data-handling standard, operating procedure, exception process
How controls, evidence, owners, and reporting are organized
What third-party risk evidence is needed?
Vendor assurance, data processing terms, incident notification, subprocessor visibility
Input classification, output validation, least privilege, logging, retention
Accountable business/risk owner, not the tool owner alone

blocks.text: Debrief prompt: ask each group which answer would satisfy an auditor, which answer would satisfy a security architect, and which answer would satisfy an executive. The difference helps students see why governance, compliance, and risk are related but not identical.
Source: CertMaster Study Lessons 2A-2C; SecurityX M02 slides.

attribution: Course: SecurityX CAS-005 Primary source: CertMaster Study Lessons 2A, 2B, 2C Slide source: SecurityX_M02_PPT.pptx Teaching goal: give students the decision language for governance, compliance, and risk before architecture topics begin.
cheatsheet: What program documents are needed?: Policy intent, data-handling standard, operating procedure, exception process
Which governance framework question matters?: How controls, evidence, owners, and reporting are organized
What compliance review is required?: Industry, privacy, contract, cross-jurisdiction, retention
What third-party risk evidence is needed?: Vendor assurance, data processing terms, incident notification, subprocessor visibility
What AI governance applies?: Input classification, output validation, least privilege, logging, retention
Who accepts residual risk?: Accountable business/risk owner, not the tool owner alone
